**What this change actually does:**

Changing the host binding from `127.0.0.1` to `0.0.0.0` makes the server listen on **all available network interfaces**, meaning:

- ❌ Anyone on the same network (LAN, Wi-Fi, VPN) can reach the server
- ❌ Depending on firewall/cloud rules, this could be **publicly internet-accessible**
- ❌ `/workspace` contents become browsable — potentially exposing **all files** in the document root, not just `resume_viewer.html`
- ❌ `SimpleHTTPRequestHandler` has **no authentication, no TLS, no access controls**

**If your team genuinely needs shared access, here are safer alternatives:**

| Approach | How | Security Benefit |
|---|---|---|
| **SSH tunnel** | `ssh -L 3000:127.0.0.1:3000 user@server` | Each teammate tunnels securely; no open port |
| **VPN-scoped bind** | Bind to your VPN interface IP (e.g. `10.x.x.x`) instead of `0.0.0.0` | Limits access to VPN members only |
| **Reverse proxy + auth** | Nginx/Caddy in front with HTTP basic auth + TLS | Adds authentication and encryption |
| **Firewall rules first** | If you must bind `0.0.0.0`, restrict the port via `iptables`/security groups to known IPs | Limits who can reach the open port |
